name: Synapse

paper.title: Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory for Computer Control

construction.unit: exemplar: task-metadata key mapped to full successful trajectories (clean observation, action pairs) and, on MiniWoB++, state-abstraction prompts
construction.kept_as: demonstrations kept as given: hand-written MiniWoB++ trajectories with human-cleaned observations; Mind2Web training trajectories with ranker top-3 observations and gold actions
construction.processing: embed each key (task text plus first HTML state, or website/domain/subdomain/task) with text-embedding-ada-002 into FAISS
construction.writer: humans and the Mind2Web training set; the agent never writes

organization.stores: one FAISS index per benchmark: MiniWoB++ 240 keys (48 tasks x 5 seeds) mapped to 48 exemplar sets; Mind2Web 1,009 training trajectories

retrieval.query: MiniWoB++: task text + initial raw HTML state; Mind2Web: website, domain, subdomain and task
retrieval.selection: MiniWoB++: majority task name among the 3, then all exemplars of that task; Mind2Web: the 3 trajectories, later ones dropped if they overflow the context

use.context: retrieved exemplar trajectories, then the task and the current trajectory of clean observations and actions
use.reasoning: per step: one state-abstraction call (LLM, LLM-written code, or the Mind2Web ranker) and one acting call that may emit several actions

classify.note: The store is built once from demonstrations and never changes at test time; 'append-only' is the closest level. On MiniWoB++ a majority vote over the top 3 picks one task whose exemplars are all used.

stages.ingestion: Demonstrations are collected before evaluation: hand-made MiniWoB++ trajectories for 48 tasks (observations cleaned by humans, parsing code sampled from GPT-4 and checked) and the 1,009 Mind2Web training tasks.
stages.construction: Each exemplar keeps a complete trajectory (task, clean observation, action, ..., observation, action); on Mind2Web the observations are the element ranker's top 3 elements. The key is task metadata embedded with text-embedding-ada-002.
stages.organization: Keys go into one FAISS index per benchmark; each key points to its exemplar (MiniWoB++: 5 keys per task from 5 random seeds).
stages.retrieval: At the start of a task its metadata is embedded and the 3 nearest keys (Euclidean) are found. MiniWoB++ takes the most common task among them and loads all its exemplars; Mind2Web uses the 3 trajectories.
stages.answer: At every step the LLM first abstracts the raw state into a short observation, then reads the exemplar trajectories plus the current task history and writes the next action(s), possibly several before asking for a new state.

summary: Computer-control agent that prompts with whole trajectories of abstracted states and actions, picked from a FAISS memory of demonstrations by similarity of task metadata instead of a hard-coded task-to-exemplar map.
notes: Venue: ICLR 2024 poster (PDF header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024'; iclr.cc/virtual/2024/poster/18701; README links openreview Pc8AU1aF5e). Text read from arXiv v3 (19 Jan 2024). Code: github.com/ltzheng/Synapse at HEAD 08c3a25 (2026-01-07); the last .py change is 89dbbf8 (2024-03-05), so the code at HEAD is the code after the camera-ready. The memory is a read-only exemplar library, not a record of the agent's own experience: management fields are null and timing none. control.construction=none because demonstrations are prepared by humans / the dataset, not by the system.

sources.code_note: Official repository linked from the paper's project page. HEAD 08c3a25 (2026-01-07) is used; commits after 2024-03-05 only touch figures and the licence, so the Python code is the post-camera-ready release. Memory contents for MiniWoB++ (specifiers.json, exemplars.json) are in the repo; the Mind2Web memory is built by build_memory.py from the dataset.

headline: The memory holds demonstrations prepared before evaluation, not the agent's own experience; nothing is written back during or after a task.
Retrieval runs once per task, on task metadata; the retrieved trajectories stay fixed for every step of the episode.
On MiniWoB++ the 3 nearest keys only vote for a task name; the agent then gets every exemplar of that task, as a hard-coded map would.

open_questions: MiniWoB++ has no memory-off ablation: the gain of memory is shown only as solving 16 unseen tasks, where the code's no-memory mode maps tasks to exemplars by hand.
On Mind2Web memory adds little (Step SR +1.4 / +1.5 / +0.2 with GPT-3.5); the static baseline uses 3 random training trajectories, so the test is similar vs random exemplars.

discussion.takeaway: Cleaning states so that whole trajectories fit in context, and choosing those trajectories by task similarity, lets an in-context agent reach 99.2% on MiniWoB++ without self-correction; memory is the smallest of the three gains on Mind2Web.

claims.claim: First ICL method at human level on MiniWoB++.
claims.evidence: 99.2% mean over 64 tasks vs human 93.5%, RCI 90.6% (54 tasks), AdaPlanner 92.9% (53). Table 3, Fig. 3

claims.claim: State abstraction makes long pages solvable and leaves room for more exemplars.
Trajectory exemplars cut error build-up on long tasks.
claims.evidence: guess-number / use-spinner / use-autocomplete 100 / 100 / 98% vs RCI 20 / 88 / 58%; Mind2Web Step SR +19% over abstraction only. §4.5, Table 1

claims.claim: Exemplar memory generalises to unseen tasks.
claims.evidence: 16 unseen MiniWoB++ tasks solved at almost 100%; Mind2Web Step SR +1.4 / +1.5 / +0.2 (GPT-3.5). §4.5, Table 2

claims.claim: 56% relative Step SR gain over MindAct on Mind2Web.

limits: High inference latency from LLM calls.
Depends on the quality of the exemplars.
Memory structure and retrieval are left for further study.
Text-only; no multimodal or pixel-based control.
reading: The memory is a curated demonstration library built before evaluation; the agent does not store its own successes, so 'memory' here means exemplar selection.

On MiniWoB++ retrieval is a vote for a task name; with a clear task split this reproduces a task-to-exemplar map automatically. There is no MiniWoB++ run that swaps memory for a hand map, so its effect is shown only on the 16 unseen tasks.
On Mind2Web the memory gain is small (Step SR +0.2 to +1.5 with GPT-3.5; -0.2 cross-domain with CodeLlama), and the no-memory variant uses 3 random training trajectories.

In code, Mind2Web history observations always include the gold element and history actions are gold, so each step is scored with a teacher-forced history; this is how the static dataset is used, not an online run.
State abstraction runs only on 20 MiniWoB++ tasks in the code; the rest act on raw HTML.
Baseline MiniWoB++ averages cover different task sets (64 vs 104 vs 54 tasks), so the averages are not directly comparable.

abstract.text: Synapse is an in-context computer-control agent built from three parts. State abstraction shrinks raw HTML to the parts a task needs, so several complete demonstrations fit in the prompt. Trajectory-as-exemplar prompting shows the LLM whole successful trajectories of observations and actions and lets it continue the current one. An exemplar memory embeds task metadata and retrieves the closest demonstrations, so tasks without their own demonstrations can borrow from similar ones. The authors report 99.2% mean success on 64 MiniWoB++ tasks with demonstrations for 48, and a 56% relative step-success gain over MindAct on Mind2Web.
